text: Given valid connector credentials in headers, When tools/list is called, Then the server returns exactly the 6 named tools, each readOnlyHint: true
Given 60 mocked upstream extension records, When yeastar_list_extensions() is called with default limit, Then it returns 50 items and has_more: true
Given a PBX with 0 extensions configured, When yeastar_list_extensions() is called, Then it returns items: [] and has_more: false, not a not_found error

Given one mocked peer-type trunk and one mocked account-type trunk, When yeastar_list_trunks() is called, Then peer fields (host_port, def_outbound_cid) and account fields (username) are both mapped correctly
Given a mocked inbound route with default/business-hours/after-hours/holiday destinations, When yeastar_list_inbound_routes() is called, Then all four destination fields are present in the result
Given a mocked outbound route list, When yeastar_list_outbound_routes() is called, Then the route fields are returned unmodified in shape
Given a mocked IVR list, When yeastar_list_ivrs() is called, Then the IVR entries are returned
Given a mocked CDR response, When yeastar_list_cdr() is called with no arguments, Then the upstream call used sort_by=time&order_by=desc and the result paginates the same way as the other list tools
Given the built tool description for yeastar_list_cdr, When it is read, Then it states there is no server-side time-range filter and that callers should page through time-sorted results
expect: Description text explicitly says there is no start/end time filter and recommends paging through time-sorted (desc) results to narrow a window
evidence: Live tools/list call (2026-11-04, local server + placeholder headers) returned for yeastar_list_cdr: description = "List call detail records (CDR) from this PBX, newest first by default. The PBX has no server-side time-range filter: to look at a specific window, page through these time-sorted results and stop once the `time` field falls outside the window you care about." -- matches expect.

text: Given a request missing only X-Yeastar-Client-Secret, When any tool is called, Then the server returns 401 and the body names exactly that header
Given a request missing all three required headers, When any tool is called, Then the server returns 401 and the body names all three
Given a mocked get_token response with errcode 10005 (ACCESS DENIED), When any tool is called, Then it returns {"error":{"code":"unauthorized","retryable":false}}

Given a mocked data call returning errcode 10004 once, then a fresh token exchange and a retried data call returning errcode 0, When a tool is called, Then it succeeds and exactly one retry was performed

Given a mocked data call returning errcode 10004 on both the original attempt and the one retry, When a tool is called, Then it returns unauthorized and the upstream was called exactly twice (no infinite loop)

Given a mocked connection timeout to the PBX, When a tool is called, Then it returns {"error":{"code":"upstream_error","retryable":true}} and the message contains neither the client secret nor any access token from the test fixtures
Given a mocked unrecognized errcode (99999), When a tool is called, Then it maps to upstream_error without raising an unhandled exception

Given two concurrent simulated requests carrying different base_url/client_id/client_secret header sets, When both are in flight at once, Then neither request's credentials or result data appear in the other's ContextVar scope, result, or logs
Given a PBX with 0 trunks configured, When yeastar_list_trunks() is called, Then it returns items: [] and has_more: false, not an error

Given a real Yeastar P-Series appliance and real credentials, When initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call is run for each of the 6 tools, Then the real response field names match what this design assumed from the public docs
